title: Amending the Obex Artifact can require the active support of as little as 5% of circulating token supply
content:
A.6.1.1.5.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 sets the approval test: "The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have 50% of votes in favor to be approved."

The two thresholds compound rather than reinforce. At exactly quorum, a bare majority is 5% of circulating supply voting yes — the minimum coalition that can change the Agent's governing document. The three-day window compresses the time available for an opposing coalition to organise past that.

This is a common and largely deliberate trade-off in token governance: high quorums cause paralysis, so designers accept minority rule in exchange for the system remaining able to act. What makes it tolerable here is the preceding filter — the Facilitator's alignment review means the 5% coalition can only pass changes already judged consistent with the Sky Core Atlas and the Obex Artifact.

That interaction is the real structure of the amendment power. The alignment gate constrains *what* can pass; the numeric thresholds only determine *whether* something already permitted does. A reader assessing capture risk should therefore weigh the Facilitator role far more heavily than the vote arithmetic — and note that turnout, not opposition, is the binding constraint on a well-organised holder.
description: The Snapshot poll runs three days and needs 10% of circulating supply participating with 50% of votes in favour
